claims.statement: packages/server/src/index.ts is the single server entrypoint: main() wires boot in a fixed order (installOutboundGuard → initializeDatabase → LoopService.recoverInterruptedRuns → profile-gated bootstrap incl. LoopDaemon → AuthService/bootstrapAdmin → middleware chain with /github/webhook before express.json() → WebSocketService → Dennis timer + /metrics + RuntimeGovernanceService + ExecutionEngine.recoverInterruptedTasks → RIR resumeInterruptedRuns in autonomous → learning services → default-off schedulers → /api router → /explore public routes → dashboard static serving → errorHandler → listen → SIGTERM handler), and any uncaught failure from main() exits the process with code 1.

DJIMITFLO_RUNTIME_PROFILE resolves to 'api' (default, also for invalid values), 'operator', or 'autonomous'; operator-capable profiles (operator and autonomous) get initOperatorServices, the Dennis governed-queue 60 s timer (which also ticks DjimitSec scan triggers), RetentionService + CognitiveLoopClosureService, and the Telegram gateway, while only 'autonomous' additionally gets experiment period-boundary recording, initAutonomousServices(db, recoverySvc), the LoopDaemon, post-recovery resumeInterruptedRuns, MetaOrchestrationService + SelfModificationPipeline, and the OpenMythos nightly scheduler.

initializeDatabase() applies a staged backup restore (restore-pending.json marker atomically renames a staged DB over the target and records a restore_completed audit event), opens better-sqlite3 at DB_PATH/DJIMITFLO_DB (default <monorepo>/.data/djimitflo.sqlite), sets foreign_keys=ON and journal_mode=WAL, then runs pre-schema migrations, both schemas, post-schema migrations, and ensureDatabaseInstanceId before any service is constructed.

At boot the in-memory lease registry (RuntimeLeaseRegistry) is empty, so LoopService.recoverInterruptedRuns (delegating to LoopRecoveryService) marks every DB-'running' worker lease without a live lease 'failed' with reason server_restart and every active loop run without a live lease 'interrupted' with reason server_restart; runs in 'planning', remote gym runs, runs already re-queued by an earlier boot's resumeInterruptedRuns, and runs whose goal is blocked awaiting a human approval are deliberately left alone, a local zombie 'running' run whose last activity predates this boot is instead settled (run interrupted, prepared leases cancelled with deploy_restart, goal failed, in-flight proposal infra_failed), and orphaned worktrees older than the LOOP_WORKTREE_MAX_AGE_HOURS (24 h) grace are pruned in the same LoopService call. The operation is idempotent and never dispatches work.

ExecutionEngine.recoverInterruptedTasks() is startup-only reconciliation that never replays work, kills unknown PIDs, or clears recovery holds automatically: it fails only confirmed in-process mock executions (metadata execution_recovery_attempt stamp correlated with the latest engine-authored 'admitted' execution_event, executorKind mock, inProcess true, sandboxed false) and pauses everything else with execution_recovery_hold: true and outcome 'unknown', requiring operator reconciliation before redispatch (executeTask rejects held tasks with EXECUTION_RECOVERY_REQUIRED and reserved provenance keys are stripped from user metadata writes so the hold cannot be forged).

The Express middleware chain is security-order-sensitive: trust proxy=1 (required for express-rate-limit behind one nginx hop), securityHeaders, requestContext (X-Request-ID), cors, then the GitHub webhook router at /github/webhook mounted BEFORE express.json() because its HMAC signature check needs the exact raw wire bytes (express.raw with inflate:false), then express.json() and requestLogger; the public /health endpoint reports build identity including commit_matches_build plus fleet_drift.

The WebSocket server is created on the shared HTTP server at path /ws with handleProtocols echoing the client's 'bearer.<token>' subprotocol per RFC 6455 §4.2.2, and WebSocketService authenticates every connection by verifying the JWT via AuthService, rejecting unauthenticated/expired/inactive-user connections with WS_CLOSE_CODES.AUTH_* close codes.

A single persistent RuntimeGovernanceService is constructed and start()ed (subscribing to swarmEventBus for behavioral monitoring) before the ExecutionEngine, which receives it as a constructor argument, and the same instance is passed to createRoutes so the engine, task dispatch, and the runtime-governance routes share one authority; learning services (MemorySyncService, ReasoningBankService with VectorMemoryService, TrajectoryStore, and MetaOrchestrationService in autonomous profiles) attach to the engine via post-construction setter calls, and MetaOrchestrationService also attaches to the shared recovery LoopService.

createRoutes builds the /api router from a declarative mount table where registration order matters: it requires auth service and middleware (throws AUTH_MIDDLEWARE_REQUIRED otherwise), limits bodies to 1 MB, re-applies securityHeaders and a 300 req/min rate limit, mounts /swarms/spawns (accepting a scoped X-Spawn-Token for runtime children) before the generic /swarms requireAuth mount, mounts unguarded signed runtime callbacks at /swarm-v2/social-runtime before /swarms, mounts self-authenticating diff routes at '/' without a mount-level guard so they don't intercept the Telegram webhook, adds usage telemetry plus authenticated /telemetry endpoints, and generates a cached authenticated openapi.json derived from the same table via mountRoutes/collectRoutes.

In operator-capable profiles the TelegramGatewayService is dynamically imported from @djimitflo/telegram and startAll()ed only when TELEGRAM_BOTS_CONFIG is set, and the instance is retained so SIGTERM can call stopAll() to release bot file leases — otherwise a restart sees EEXIST and skips polling forever; in-memory default-off schedulers (compliance reports, self-healing, self-improvement auto-review, frontier experts, specialist-panel backlog, memory candidate review, dependency lane, Ollama failover probe, shipped-code scan, skill distillation, content drafts, content-safety retry) are armed via start() methods that no-op unless their enable env var is set, and each arms through noteScheduler plus a registerRestart bounded self-heal rearm hook.

Before main() runs, module-level code derives a default DJIMITFLO_CONTROL_URL of http://<dialHost>:<PORT>/api/swarms/spawns (rewriting the 0.0.0.0/localhost bind address to loopback 127.0.0.1 because a bind address is not a dial address) so same-host runtime children can call back to the nested-spawn endpoint without operator configuration, and logs the anti-agentic ransomware module mode (RANSOMWARE_MODULE_ENABLED default on, RANSOMWARE_MODULE_MODE default 'detect').

bootstrapAdmin() creates the bootstrap admin from AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL/PASSWORD if not already present; when no users exist and no bootstrap credentials are configured it calls process.exit(1) in production but only warns in other environments.

The production dashboard is served from DASHBOARD_PATH (default packages/dashboard/dist) via express.static plus an SPA fallback answering index.html only for GET requests with Accept: text/html that are not under /api, /ws, or /health; DASHBOARD_SERVE_ENABLED=false or a missing dist directory puts the server into API-only mode. The errorHandler is registered last and maps error codes to HTTP statuses via pattern inference.

On SIGTERM the entrypoint stops the ExplainerFleetWorker, gracefully closes every upgraded WebSocket client with code 1001 ('Server shutting down') so httpServer.close() is not blocked, terminates surviving sockets after a 5-second unref'd deadline, closes the WebSocket server, clears the Dennis queue timer, calls telegramGateway.stopAll() to release leases, and then closes the HTTP server, clears the deadline, closes the database, and exits 0. This entrypoint installs no SIGINT handler and does not use the standalone LifecycleManager's signal wiring.

Boot is tolerant of secondary failures — loop recovery, LoopDaemon start, recordTreatmentEnvBoundaries, ExplainerFleetWorker start, Telegram init, and each autonomous-service block each log a warning and continue — while database initialization, JWT_SECRET absence in production, production admin bootstrap (no users and no bootstrap env), the createRoutes AUTH_MIDDLEWARE_REQUIRED guard, and an uncaught main() error are hard failures that exit the process with code 1.

The ExplainerFleetWorker runs in every runtime profile (moved out of the autonomous-only branch so explainer jobs do not idle in api/operator mode), can be opted out with DJIMITFLO_EXPLAINER_AUTONOMY=false, and honors the kill-switch.

Focused tests pin the startup contract: server-startup.test.ts constructs the DB, core services, auth middleware, full route tree and bootstrapAdmin in-process; e2e-smoke.test.ts spawns the real src/index.ts on a temp database and drives login, WebSocket handshake, task creation, mock-executor execution and completion over the wire; task-recovery.test.ts and loop-recovery-service.test.ts / loop-recovery-awaiting-approval.test.ts verify the recovery invariants.

At module scope, before main(), installOutboundGuard wraps globalThis.fetch so every in-process fetch to a host in OUTBOUND_DENY_HOSTS (exact, subdomain, or first-label MagicDNS match) is rejected with OUTBOUND_DENIED before a socket opens; once the database is initialized main() hands the guard the db handle so refusals are also recorded as policy_violations rows (outbound_denied, deduped one per host per hour).

In autonomous profiles, after both loop recovery and the engine's recoverInterruptedTasks reconciliation, main() calls recoverySvc.resumeInterruptedRuns() (LOOP_RESUME_INTERRUPTED, default off; shadow records per-candidate judgments only): each run this boot interrupted with server_restart gets one fresh prepared maker via retryLoopRun and its goal returns to 'decomposed' with metadata.resume_run_id so the LoopDaemon's next tick runs it through every gate again, subject to a strict blocker list (operator pause, execution_recovery_hold, remote run, resume_attempts >= 3, non-running goal, non-executing proposal, unknown task outcome, completed maker).

The LoopDaemon is constructed with the same LoopService instance used for boot recovery (new LoopDaemon(db, recoverySvc)) so the daemon, initAutonomousServices, and resumeInterruptedRuns share one runtime-lease view; its start() restores persisted active goals from system_state and polls the goal queue at GOAL_QUEUE_POLL_MS (default 5000 ms), and a daemon start failure is non-fatal.

SIGTERM shutdown in index.ts stops the ExplainerFleetWorker, drains upgraded WebSocket clients with close(1001) plus a 5 s unref'd terminate deadline, clears the Dennis queue timer, calls telegramGateway.stopAll() fire-and-forget, then httpServer.close() followed by db.close() and process.exit(0); there is no SIGINT handler and no HTTP drain timeout in this entrypoint, unlike the standalone LifecycleManager which force-resolves server.close after 10 s and stops registered services in reverse order on SIGTERM/SIGINT.
